subject: Interested in Redwood — GitHub integration questions / demo
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@openlib.dev>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interested in Redwood - GitHub integration questions

Hi Camila,

I signed up for Redwood's free tier after reading about the GitHub integration on your docs. We're evaluating how to add automated code-review comments and PR annotation using an LLM. A few quick questions:

- Does Redwood support sending inference requests triggered from GitHub webhooks (PR opened/updated)?
- Do you have examples for OAuth flow for GitHub when calling Redwood from CI/workflows?
- Rough pricing for demo/POC volumes (we expect 50k tokens/week at start).

Would love to set up a short demo with someone who knows the GitHub side of things - I can bring our engineering lead (Samira).

Thanks,
Alex Wu
Sr. Engineer, OpenLib
alex.wu@openlib.dev
https://openlib.dev

From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@openlib.dev>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interested in Redwood - GitHub integration questions

Hi Alex - great to meet you, and thanks for signing up!

Short answer: yes - Redwood is commonly integrated into GitHub workflows via webhooks and CI. We have patterns for both server-side webhook triggers and GitHub Actions/OAuth flows. I can put together a 30-min demo focused on the integration + recommended architecture for PR comments.

Quick availability: https://calendly.com/camila-redwood/30min - pick a time that works and I’ll add the right folks from our side (AE/SE) to the invite.

I attached our one-pager so you have a quick summary of latency/cost controls and deployment options.

Looking forward,
Camila Reyes
Sales Development Rep | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_OnePager.pdf

Thanks Camila - I booked a tentative time via Calendly but can be flexible.

A couple more specifics for the demo team so we can focus the agenda:
- Our main ask is automated PR comments with suggested code changes (private repos). Is there a recommended approach for securely invoking Redwood from GitHub Actions without exposing API keys?
- Do you support annotating suggestions inline (threaded review comments) vs posting a summary comment?
- Would love to see an example where a model is pinned to a specific quantized variant for cost reasons.

Available windows this week: 6/19 10-12 PT, 6/19 3-5 PT, 6/24 anytime morning PT (we're in PST).

Also looping in Samira (our eng lead) to confirm timing.

—Alex
